396	class _Token:
397	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
398	    value: Any
399	    text: str
400	
401	
402	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
403	    r"""
404	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
405	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
406	    """,
407	    re.VERBOSE,
408	)
409	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
410	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
411	
412	
413	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
414	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
415	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
416	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
417	    i = 0
418	    n = len(sql)
419	    while i < n:
420	        ch = sql[i]
421	        if ch.isspace():
422	            i += 1
423	            continue
424	        if ch == "*":
425	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
426	            i += 1
427	            continue
428	        if ch in ",()+-/":
429	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
430	            i += 1
431	            continue
432	        if ch in "=<>!":
433	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
434	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
435	                i += 2
436	                continue
437	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
438	                op = ch + "="
439	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
440	                i += 2
441	                continue
442	            if ch in "=<>":
443	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
444	                i += 1
445	                continue
446	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
447	        if ch == "'":
448	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
449	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
450	            i = new_i
451	            continue
452	        if ch == '"':
453	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
454	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
455	            i = new_i
456	            continue
457	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
458	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
459	            if match:
460	                text = match.group(0)
461	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
462	                i = match.end()
463	                continue
464	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
465	            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
466	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
467	            i += 1
468	            continue
469	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
470	        if match:
471	            text = match.group(0)
472	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
473	            i = match.end()
474	            continue
475	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
476	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
477	    return tokens
478	
479	
480	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
481	    lowered = word.lower()
482	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
483	        if lowered == "true":
484	            return _Token("number", True, word)
485	        if lowered == "false":
486	            return _Token("number", False, word)
487	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
488	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
489	
490	
491	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
492	    parts: list[str] = []
493	    i = start + 1
494	    n = len(sql)
495	    while True:
496	        j = sql.find("'", i)
497	        if j == -1:
498	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
499	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
500	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
501	            parts.append("'")
502	            i = j + 2
503	            continue
504	        value = "".join(parts)
505	        try:
506	            value.encode("utf-8")
507	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
508	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
509	        return value, j + 1
510	
511	
512	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
513	    parts: list[str] = []
514	    i = start + 1
515	    n = len(sql)
516	    while True:
517	        j = sql.find('"', i)
518	        if j == -1:
519	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
520	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
521	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
522	            parts.append('"')
523	            i = j + 2
524	            continue
525	        value = "".join(parts)
526	        if not value:
527	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
528	        return value, j + 1
529	
530	
531	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
532	    try:
533	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
534	            value: int | float = float(text)
535	        else:
536	            value = int(text, 10)
537	    except ValueError:
538	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
539	    if isinstance(value, int):
540	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
541	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
542	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
543	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
544	        return value
545	    if not math.isfinite(value):
546	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
547	    return value

550	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
551	# Parsed expression tree
552	#
553	# Node tuples:
554	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
555	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
556	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
557	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
558	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
559	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
560	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
561	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
562	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
563	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
564	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
565	#   ("not", operand)
566	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
567	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
568	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
569	#
570	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
571	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
572	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
573	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
574	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
575	
576	
577	@dataclass(frozen=True)
578	class _RefItem:
579	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
580	
581	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
582	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
583	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
584	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
585	    distinct: bool = False  # kind == "agg": DISTINCT before the argument
586	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
587	    descending: bool = False
588	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
589	    # Table qualifiers (multi-table queries only; None when unqualified):
590	    table: str | None = None
591	    table_quoted: bool = False
592	    arg_table: str | None = None
593	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
594	
595	
596	@dataclass(frozen=True)
597	class _Join:
598	    """One equi-join step of a multi-table query.
599	
600	    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
601	    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
602	    introduced table as its right input.
603	    """
604	
605	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left" | "right" | "full"
606	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
607	    table_quoted: bool
608	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
609	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
610	
611	
612	@dataclass
613	class _Select:
614	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
615	    table: str
616	    table_quoted: bool
617	    where: tuple | None
618	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
619	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
620	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
621	    having: tuple | None
622	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
623	    limit: int | None
624	    # Join steps in FROM/JOIN order; empty for a single-table statement.
625	    joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
626	    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
627	    distinct: bool = False
628	
629	    @property
630	    def star(self) -> bool:
631	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
632	
633	    @property
634	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
635	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
636	
637	    @property
638	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
639	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None
640

642	class _Parser:
643	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
644	
645	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
646	        self.tokens = tokens
647	        self.pos = 0
648	        # Multi-table statements (qualified names + join clauses) are only
649	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
650	        # them as syntax errors.
651	        self._allow_join = allow_join
652	
653	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
654	        select = self._parse_select()
655	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
656	            tok = self._peek()
657	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
658	        return select
659	
660	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
661	        self._expect_keyword("select")
662	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
663	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
664	        self._expect_keyword("from")
665	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
666	        joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
667	        if self._allow_join:
668	            joins = tuple(self._parse_join_clauses())
669	        where = None
670	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
671	            where = self._parse_or()
672	        group_by = None
673	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
674	            self._expect_keyword("by")
675	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
676	            while self._accept_op(","):
677	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
678	            group_by = tuple(names)
679	        having = None
680	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
681	            having = self._parse_having_or()
682	        order_by = None
683	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
684	            self._expect_keyword("by")
685	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
686	            while self._accept_op(","):
687	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
688	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
689	        limit = None
690	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
691	            limit = self._parse_limit()
692	        return _Select(
693	            items=items,
694	            table=table_tok.value,
695	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
696	            where=where,
697	            group_by=group_by,
698	            having=having,
699	            order_by=order_by,
700	            limit=limit,
701	            joins=joins,
702	            distinct=distinct,
703	        )
704	
705	    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
706	        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
707	        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
708	        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
709	        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
710	        # working outside join parsing.
711	        joins: list[_Join] = []
712	        while True:
713	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
714	                self._expect_keyword("join")
715	                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
716	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
717	                self._expect_keyword("join")
718	                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
719	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
720	                self._expect_keyword("join")
721	                joins.append(self._parse_join("right"))
722	            elif self._accept_word("full"):
723	                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted.
724	                self._expect_word("outer")
725	                self._expect_keyword("join")
726	                joins.append(self._parse_join("full"))
727	            else:
728	                return joins
729	
730	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
731	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
732	        self._expect_keyword("on")
733	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
734	        self._expect_op("=")
735	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
736	        return _Join(
737	            kind=kind,
738	            table=table_tok.value,
739	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
740	            left_key=left_key,
741	            right_key=right_key,
742	        )
743	
744	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
745	        tok = self._peek()
746	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
747	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
748	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
749	            )
750	        self._next()
751	        if not self._accept_op("."):
752	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
753	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
754	            )
755	        nxt = self._peek()
756	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
757	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
758	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
759	            )
760	        self._next()
761	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
762	
763	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
764	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
765	        while self._accept_op(","):
766	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
767	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
768	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
769	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
770	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
771	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
772	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
773	        tok = self._peek()
774	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
775	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
776	        ):
777	            grouped_ahead = any(
778	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
779	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
780	            )
781	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
782	                raise QueryValidationError(
783	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
784	                )
785	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
786	        return items
787	
788	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
789	        tok = self._peek()
790	        if tok.kind == "star":
791	            self._next()
792	            return _RefItem("star")
793	        if (
794	            tok.kind == "ident"
795	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
796	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
797	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
798	        ):
799	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
800	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
801	                raise QueryValidationError(
802	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
803	                )
804	            return item
805	        node = self._parse_arith()
806	        if node[0] == "column":
807	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
808	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
809	            return _RefItem(
810	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
811	            )
812	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
813	        self._expect_keyword("as")
814	        alias = self._peek()
815	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
816	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
817	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
818	            )
819	        self._next()
820	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
821	
822	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
823	        tok = self._peek()
824	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
825	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
826	        )
827	
828	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
829	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
830	        descending = False
831	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
832	            descending = False
833	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
834	            descending = True
835	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
836	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
837	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
838	                nulls_first = True
839	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
840	                nulls_first = False
841	            else:
842	                tok = self._peek()
843	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
844	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
845	                )
846	        return _RefItem(
847	            item.kind,
848	            name=item.name,
849	            func=item.func,
850	            arg=item.arg,
851	            distinct=item.distinct,
852	            descending=descending,
853	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
854	            table=item.table,
855	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
856	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
857	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
858	        )
859	
860	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
861	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
862	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
863	
864	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
865	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
866	        table_tok = self._next()
867	        self._expect_op(".")
868	        name_tok = self._peek()
869	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
870	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
871	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
872	            )
873	        self._next()
874	        return _RefItem(
875	            "column",
876	            name=name_tok.value,
877	            table=table_tok.value,
878	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
879	        )
880	
881	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
882	        tok = self._peek()
883	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
884	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
885	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
886	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
887	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
888	        # can only be a plain column reference.
889	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
890	            self._next()
891	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
892	        func = tok.value.lower()
893	        self._next()  # consume the function name
894	        if not self._accept_op("("):
895	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
896	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
897	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
898	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
899	        self._expect_op(")")
900	        return _RefItem(
901	            "agg",
902	            func=func.upper(),
903	            arg=arg,
904	            distinct=distinct,
905	            arg_table=arg_table,
906	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
907	        )
908	
909	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
910	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
911	        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
912	        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
913	        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
914	        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
915	        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
916	        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
917	        # opened.
918	        tok = self._peek()
919	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
920	            raise QueryValidationError(
921	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
922	            )
923	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "distinct":
924	            self._next()
925	            tok = self._peek()
926	            if tok.kind == "star":
927	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
928	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
929	                )
930	            if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
931	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
932	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
933	                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
934	                )
935	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
936	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
937	                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
938	            else:
939	                self._next()
940	                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
941	            nxt = self._peek()
942	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
943	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
944	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column name, "
945	                    "not a function call"
946	                )
947	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
948	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
949	                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
950	                    "reference, not an expression"
951	                )
952	            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
953	        if tok.kind == "star":
954	            if func != "count":
955	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
956	            self._next()
957	            return ("", None, False, False)
958	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
959	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
960	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
961	            )
962	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
963	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
964	            nxt = self._peek()
965	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
966	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
967	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
968	                )
969	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
970	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
971	        self._next()
972	        nxt = self._peek()

1312	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1313	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional

1336	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
1337	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
1338	
1339	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
1340	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1341	        self.pos += 1
1342	        return tok

1346	            self.pos += 1
1347	            return True
1348	        return False

1351	        tok = self._peek()
1352	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
1353	            self.pos += 1
1354	            return True
1355	        return False
1356	
1357	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1358	        tok = self._peek()
1359	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:

1361	            return True

1453	def _bind_plain(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
1454	    # Non-aggregate path: '*' or a comma-separated list of plain columns and
1455	    # computed scalar expressions (each named with AS).
1456	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
1457	    if select.star:
1458	        for i, col in enumerate(schema.columns):
1459	            bound_items.append(
1460	                _BoundItem(
1461	                    "column",
1462	                    output_name=col.name,
1463	                    col_index=i,
1464	                    out_type=col.type,
1465	                    nullable=col.nullable,
1466	                )
1467	            )
1468	    else:
1469	        output_seen: set[str] = set()
1470	        for item in select.items:
1471	            if item.kind == "star":
1472	                # A star mixed into a plain projection remains grammatical.
1473	                raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' cannot be mixed with other projection items")
1474	            if item.kind == "column":
1475	                name = item.name
1476	                if name in output_seen:
1477	                    raise QueryValidationError(
1478	                        f"duplicate column in projection: {name!r}"
1479	                    )
1480	                try:
1481	                    col_index = schema.index(name)
1482	                except KeyError:
1483	                    raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
1484	                col = schema.columns[col_index]
1485	                output_seen.add(col.name)
1486	                bound_items.append(
1487	                    _BoundItem(
1488	                        "column",
1489	                        output_name=col.name,
1490	                        col_index=col_index,
1491	                        out_type=col.type,
1492	                        nullable=col.nullable,
1493	                    )
1494	                )
1495	            else:  # "expr"

"""Single-file SQL query layer.

Public API:

* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement against a table-name to path
  mapping, optionally chaining several equi-joins
* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use

The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::

    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
                   [HAVING expr]
                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
                   [LIMIT uint]
    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')'
                   | scalar_expr AS alias
    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' [DISTINCT] ('*' | ident) ')')
                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
    expr       := or_expr
    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
    operand     := ident | literal
    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
                   | single-quoted utf8

The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Each of
``COUNT`` / ``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` also accepts
``DISTINCT`` before its single column argument (``COUNT(DISTINCT ident)``
etc.): rows are first selected by WHERE, then within each group (or the
single global group) NULL arguments are ignored and the remaining values
are deduplicated by the column's type -- float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0``
count as the same value -- before the aggregate runs.  ``COUNT(DISTINCT
x)`` returns the number of distinct non-NULL values (0 on empty input,
a non-nullable int64); the other DISTINCT aggregates return NULL when no
distinct non-NULL value remains and otherwise keep the result type,
nullability, comparison rules and overflow / non-finite
:class:`QueryValidationError` behaviour of their plain counterparts.
DISTINCT here only deduplicates the aggregate's argument values; it does
not change ``SELECT DISTINCT`` row deduplication, and the argument stays
a single column reference (no ``*``, expressions, multiple arguments or
nested aggregates).  A misplaced DISTINCT keyword, a missing argument,
``*``, an expression or multiple arguments inside a DISTINCT call raise
:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.  DISTINCT
aggregates may appear wherever plain aggregates may (SELECT, HAVING,
ORDER BY), and textually identical calls share one computation.  Without
GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
for bare columns or aggregate calls.

Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.

``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
:class:`QueryValidationError`; argument-level ``DISTINCT`` inside an
aggregate call (``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` etc.) is a separate feature
described above and stays an aggregate query.  A missing projection, a
repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced DISTINCT keyword raises
:class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is opened.

The row-processing stages (WHERE, the ORDER BY sort keys, the SELECT
expressions and the projection feeding SELECT DISTINCT) share one batched
column-vector evaluator: each stage hands the next a set of valid row
indices, and an expression is evaluated one batch of column values at a
time instead of row by row.  The batched semantics are exactly the
per-row semantics described above -- three-valued logic, NULL propagation,
per-row CASE short-circuit, the int64 / float64 promotion and error rules
and the stage order (so filtered or LIMIT-cut rows never evaluate the
expressions of a later stage) are unchanged.  Joins, grouping, aggregation
and HAVING keep their existing result organisation; the data they hand to
the expression stages follows the same batched semantics.

Searched CASE expressions
(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
match each other exactly (any other mix raises
:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
expressions.

Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.

After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.

Multi-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add a deterministic chain of zero
or more equi-joins to the grammar::

    query := SELECT ... FROM from_table
             { join_kind JOIN next_table
               ON (earlier_table.col = next_table.col
                   | next_table.col = earlier_table.col) } ...
    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER

``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
the statement are read.  Each join step introduces exactly one not-yet-used
table (aliases and repeated tables are rejected) and its single ON equality
connects a qualified column of that new table with a qualified column of any
table introduced earlier (FROM or a previous join); the two sides of the
equality are interchangeable.  Compound or non-equality ON conditions,
other join types and ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` are syntax errors raised
before any file is opened.  In any statement that contains a JOIN every
column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column``
(either part may be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the
referenced schemas in FROM/JOIN order with ``table.column`` names; explicit
projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.

Each step is evaluated with the materialised intermediate result as its
left input and the newly read table as its right input.  Join keys may
share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN
emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows
with the right-side values set to NULL (the new table's result columns are
nullable), RIGHT JOIN emits all new-table rows in new-file order (one new
row's matches expand in intermediate/current row order) padding the whole
intermediate side with NULL (every earlier table's result columns become
nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and then appends
the unmatched new rows in new-file order (every result column is nullable).
INNER / LEFT / FULL expand in the current intermediate row order, with the
matching new rows in new-file order within one current row; RIGHT expands
in new-file row order with the matches in current row order.  Nullability
is derived per step: once a step makes an earlier table's columns
nullable, later steps keep them nullable.  WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
projection / DISTINCT / stable sorting / LIMIT run only after the whole
chain has been built, with their usual semantics.

The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``; an
explicit strategy is applied to every join step.  Both strategies accept
the same statements and return identical column descriptions, values, NULL
placement and row order; they differ only in how matching right rows are
located (a right-key hash index versus sorting both sides on the key and
merging equal-key runs).  With the argument omitted the historical
default join path is used and the explain plan carries no strategy field;
with an explicit strategy every plan Join operator gains a ``strategy``
field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement accepts either
strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid strategy raises
:class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.

The explain plan lists the referenced sources and their Scan operators in
FROM/JOIN order with ``required_columns`` attributed to each source, then
one Join operator per step in the same order, recording the step type and
the two normalised qualified keys (the earlier table on the left, the
freshly introduced table on the right).

Row-group-partitioned (v2) files are read selectively: every query decodes
only the column blocks its plan actually references (a join chain
additionally reads each table's ON keys).  Single-file statements
(:func:`query_file` and JOIN-less :func:`query_files`) and multi-file
statements whose whole join chain is INNER push the AND-connected,
type-compatible comparisons and IS [NOT] NULL conditions of WHERE down to
the per-group statistics.  In a join chain only a top-level AND leaf that
references exactly one source (a qualified column of that source compared
to a type-compatible literal, on either side, or that column's IS [NOT]
NULL) is attributed to that source; each source's own leaves are combined
with AND independently.  A chain containing any LEFT / RIGHT / FULL OUTER
step performs no row-group pruning at all (an OUTER step can pad a source
with NULLs, so no group can be proven absent), v1 sources are always read
in full, and in a mixed v1/v2 all-INNER chain only the v2 sources are
pruned.

A row group is skipped only when a source's statistics prove its pushed
leaves cannot all be TRUE at once for any of the group's rows; OR, NOT,
CASE, arithmetic, column-to-column or cross-source comparisons and
undecidable ranges are never pushed, and neither block nor replace the
eligible leaves next to them.  Surviving rows are still filtered row by
row with the full WHERE condition over the complete join result, so NULL
three-valued logic, duplicate key combinations, aggregates, DISTINCT,
ordering, LIMIT and the deterministic unordered row order are unchanged.
When every group is excluded the statement simply sees zero rows, so
empty results, ``COUNT(*)``, other global aggregates and HAVING keep
their usual semantics.  Both format versions return identical column
descriptions, values, row order, sorting, LIMIT, join and export results
for the same data and statement.  Only the blocks of the columns and row
groups actually selected are decompressed or decoded: a block belonging
to an excluded group is never read even when corrupt, while a corrupt
block of a selected group raises
:class:`~columnar_analytics.format.ColumnarFormatError`.

In the explain plan a v2 Scan operator of an eligible statement
(single-source, or an all-INNER chain) carries, right after
``required_columns``, the fields ``row_groups_total``,
``row_groups_selected`` and ``pushed_condition`` (the leaves attributed
to that source combined, in SQL appearance order, as one condition tree
with qualified column names, or null when no leaf was pushed; with no
pushed leaf selected equals total).  v1 Scan operators and the Scan
operators of a chain containing an OUTER step keep their historical
shape; the reported counts always match the groups execution reads.
"""
